newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan greets Bangladesh on independence day.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan greets Bangladesh on independence day.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari said he was confident ties with Dhaka would go from strength to strength as Bangladesh marked its 26th anniversary of independence from Pakistan on Wednesday.

"The existing ties of close friendship, cooperation and mutual understanding between Pakistan and Bangladesh are a reflection of our shared history and common faith," Leghari said in his message to President Shahabuddin Ahmed.
"I am confident that these bonds will continue to grow from strength to strength in the years ahead for the mutual benefit of our two peoples," Leghari said.
Bangladesh, formerly East Pakistan, proclaimed independence on March 26, 1971, and gained its freedom on December 16 after a nine-month war in which it received help from India.
Relations between Pakistan and Bangladesh in general have greatly improved since the trauma of secession.
But Dhaka's recent proposal for a sub-regional grouping, excluding Pakistan, within the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) has made Islamabad uneasy.
Bangladesh wants to get together with India, Nepal and Bhutan for cooperation, particularly on water resources, but Pakistan feels the move could isolate it within SAARC.
Indian-Pakistani rivalry has long hindered the development of the seven-nation SAARC as an engine for regional trade and economic growth.
